newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak shares quiet, SAX eases 0.07 pts to 168.85.
newsitem.headline: Slovak shares quiet, SAX eases 0.07 pts to 168.85.

text.p: Slovak blue chips were mostly steady in listless trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, as the 16-share SAX index dipped 0.07 points to 168.85.
Trading on the BSE's listed floor was dominated by steel maker VSZ, which traded 9,611 shares, closing unchanged at 633 crowns.
Other blue chips either traded insignificant volumes or did not match any shares due to a lack of investor interest, which brokers predicting the bearish sentiment to last into the autumn.
Oil refinery Slovnaft, Slovakia's leading issue, did not trade on Tuesday, staying unchanged at 860 crowns.
Dealers said the cheapest Slovnaft offer was at 870, while the highest bids touched only 850 crowns.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta closed down 59 crowns at 1,050 but traded only two shares.

Tuesday's volume and turnover on the BSE were boosted by direct deals in Novacke chemicke zavody, where 813,485 shares were matched at 1,496 crowns. The issue traded 10 shares on the bourse's unlisted floor, at 240 crowns.
Overall, volume climbed to 1,142,800 shares, from 359,662 shares traded on Monday, while turnover rose to 1.274 billion crowns from 147.93 million.
